intro: The forty-fifth screen read 87 pictures, the set's 21 and 66 probes, with eleven readers and four scorers: 939 of 971 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. **The walker about to trip, which failed the last two gates, reads in full in all five of its pictures, and one other template fails.** The set's overall score is 0.993, from 0.991, the highest of the last five sets, and 63 of the 64 templates pass the gate, as in v0.47. The one that fails is `rain_coming` (0.889 in three pictures): one reader named the storm clouds and the child pointing at them and did not go on to the rain. Nothing of that template was changed in this release but the figure who points. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one, and the rain heads the list for v0.49. Of the drawing, the bench is the evidence: beside v0.47's, the new people were the better drawn in 12 pairs of 16 on the last of three benches, and the new dogs and cats in 14 of 15. In the screen every dog, cat, goat and duck is named for what it is in every picture it is in, and the scorers logged 2 oddities in the set for v0.47's 7. Two things stand against the better numbers. The finer faces cost two readings v0.47's had: no reader named a moustache or a beard, and four grown figures are called a girl or a boy in 11 of their 81 pictures, for 6 of 80. And many full marks still carry a hedge: on the strict count 55 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.47's 56. Twenty-three of the 32 items under full marks are clouds or a tree that two readers left out.
design:
## Design tests

The cast of builder 0.48.0 and revision 45's rules were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v048.md`, eight pictures, one fresh reader each). The bench had read the figures one at a time and in pairs; this was the first time a reader had them at a picture's size. Between them the eight forced sets hold every person of the cast, every animal that was redrawn and six templates of the v0.47 list. Six placed on their first seed and two on their second. No picture was built again, before a reading or after one.

Every forced event was read, twenty-four of twenty-four. That is a count of what a reader wrote about a picture built to show the event; it is not the screen, where a scorer who has not seen the picture marks each item against the description. What the readers wrote:
- **The walker and the box:** "an older man in a grey cap, brown waistcoat and dark trousers is hurrying along to the right (motion lines behind him) with his eyes down on an open book he holds in both hands." The direction came with no hedge.
- **The dog on the hose:** "a tan dog with a red collar is standing right on top of the hose (at what looks like a joint or bulge in it) next to the flower bed, so it seems the dog is pinching off the water."
- **The reading dog:** "That dog reading a newspaper is the oddest thing in the picture, since dogs cannot read."
- **The cat and the bird:** "an orange cat is crouched low, stalking toward the right with its tail stretched out behind it."
- **The begging dog:** "A brown puppy with a red collar sits up on its hind legs in front of him, begging and looking up at his ice cream."
- **The goat:** "a white goat with curved horns and a red collar is grazing on a tuft of grass; it is tied by a rope to a small wooden stake in the ground".
- **The cast.** The older woman was "an elderly woman with grey hair in a bun and glasses", both named with no doubt. No reader named a head's shape, a neck, a shoulder, a stiff leg or a shadow.

What the tests showed first, and the screen then counted: three grown people were read young. The woman in the yellow dress was "a woman in a yellow dress" carrying a box and "a girl in a yellow dress" feeding the birds; the bearded man in green was "a boy in a green shirt" on a bench, his beard unnamed; and of the woman in purple, "The person watering could be read as an adult woman or a teenage girl." None of the three readers of the older man named his moustache. Nothing was mended after the readings; each remark went to the screen as it stood.
redrawn: `about_to_trip` failed v0.47's gate and reads 1.00 in five pictures; four of its fifteen full marks stand beside "might pass just beside it". The six templates under it on v0.47's list were not worked, and they carry the redrawn animals and figures: `blocked_hose` reads 0.95 in five, on two half marks for "the tap is off"; `lost_balloon` 0.933 in five, on two; `bird_steals` 0.972 in six, on one; `water_upward`, `cat_stalks_bird` and `dog_reading` 1.00 in five each. It is one screen, of 15 to 20 items a template, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.025 to 0.033. Where a redrawn animal carries a plain event the reading held: `walk_dog` 1.00 in six pictures, `dog_sleeping` in five, `dog_begs` in four, `dog_playing` in four, `goat_grazing` in four, `cat_on_fence` and `cat_sleeping` in three each. `ice_cream` fell from 1.00 to 0.95 over twenty pictures, on two walkers whose cone was held up and not seen at the mouth, and eight more of its full marks are calls of the same kind: the new face's mouth is lower and plain, and the cone stops short of it. `rain_coming`, not worked, fell from 1.00 to 0.889 on one unsaid inference and fails.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (37 in three, 11 in four, 10 in five, 3 in six, 1 in eight, 1 in eleven and 1 in twenty), and 63 of the 64 pass, as in v0.47. The one that fails is in the table below: `rain_coming`, 0.889 on nine items in three pictures, with no misread. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. The lowest that pass are `lost_balloon` (0.933), `ducks_bread` (0.944), `blocked_hose` and `ice_cream` (0.95) and `bird_steals` (0.972); the other 58 read 1.00, among them `about_to_trip`, which failed the last two gates. Per angle (`vision/v048/gate_yaw.json`), 19 of the 19 (template, angle) pairs pass, as in v0.47, eighteen at 1.00 and the thief bird in profile at 0.917. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 33 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 55 of the 64 pass. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
calib: With the cast drawn again and revision 45's first two rules, 51 of the calibration's 252 numbers moved, most of all `dog_reading`'s contradiction (s from -0.397 to -0.299) and `dog_begs`'s inference (-0.872 to -0.791), both on the new dog, and the planner's priors moved with them. One rule came after the calibration: `REEL48`, found on the look at the set, which keeps animals off the garden's hose reel. It touches only an animal that would have stood over the reel, in the garden; every other record of the set rebuilds to the pixel with it, and `calibration.json` and the priors are left as measured without it.
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 45, with the priors of the cast's new drawing, and it took less searching than v0.47's. In tiers 1 and 2, five cells placed on their base seed and two on its second step; the tier-2 park failed two bases and placed on a third. In tier 3 all four cells placed on the showcase's own seeds: the garden on its second step, the street on its first (v0.47 had needed a second base), the playground on its eighth (v0.47's was forced) and the park on its seventeenth. In tier 4 the park and the playground placed on v0.47's seeds with v0.47's templates, and the garden on the thirty-fourth seed of the search, after v0.47's and thirty-two more had failed. The tier-4 street was built from v0.47's forced set: the set that holds the walker about to trip placed on none of eight seeds, every one of its 112 layouts failing on the walker, who wants a clear stretch behind and ahead and now room for his motion lines. Six cells have v0.47's templates and ten have others. **I looked at every picture of the set before any reader had it, and one was wrong:** in a tier-2 isomorph the begging dog sat up in front of the garden's hose reel with its head on the drum. `REEL48` came of it; that isomorph no longer builds and was taken out, and the other twenty-one records rebuild to the pixel with the rule. The isomorphs are five again: three of tier 2, one of tier 3 and one of tier 4, the last found on the third call of a wider search, on v0.47's seed, after 65 calls of the plain one had found none. The probe pass built 54 and gave up the windblown hat after three failures that were its partners', the pass stratified by angle added 10, and two more were forced with the hat in small groups: 66 probes, 34 gardens, 22 parks, 10 playgrounds and no street. Every probe was looked at on sheets of four before the screen, and none was built again after that look. All 87 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 352 of 352. Its soft palette warning is raised by 283 records (169 of 390 in v0.47): the redrawn figures carry more inner line, at the animals' joints and along a hairline, and what is off the palette is the blended band where a line meets a fill. The target was not loosened.
